query: Hey folks, quick question - we're seeing some weird routing behavior where deep links work fine on mobile but break on web. Anyone dealt with go_router handling links differently across platforms? Specifically around email verification flows?
chunk_content:
I’m dealing with what seems to be a difference in behavior between web and mobile platforms in go_router. I’m trying to implement a system to add email addresses to a user’s profile using deep links. So the general process is like so:
- the user asks to add an email address to their profile
- the backend sends that email address a link with a unique code in a link
- the user clicks that link that opens the app that processes the deep link by verifying the code and finishing to add the verified email address to the user profile

The problem is in the last step: as I’m using app_links, per the documentation, I disabled Android’s flutter_deeplinking_enabled and iOS’s FlutterDeepLinkingEnabled, so I think that’s why when I click the deep link on iOS or Android, the deep link URL with a path like /verify-email?code=123 is not forwarded to go_router unless I explicitly call goRouter.go(path). But on the web, it seems like my deep link is instantly forwarded to go_router, which results in a 404 error since I don’t have any route configured for /verify-email.

So in the end, my mechanism works on Android and iOS, but fails miserably on the web. How should I do this?

chunk_content:
Secure connection over ESP32 with Flutter using Security 2 (SRP6) fails – “Failed to authenticate client proof! Invalid username/PoP

I’m working on connecting a Flutter app to an ESP32 device over BLE using the ESP-IDF provisioning/security scheme 2 (SRP6).

However, the connection fails with the following error messages from the ESP32 logs:

E (xxxxx) security2: Failed to authenticate client proof! E (xxxxx) security2: Received incorrect username and/or PoP for establishing secure session! E (xxxxx) protocomm: Invalid content received, killing connection

What I’ve done:

Using Flutter with flutter_blue_plus to handle BLE communication.

Converted the SRP6 client implementation from Java to Dart to generate A, M, and proof values.

I am passing the correct PoP (same as configured in ESP32) and the salt provided by the device.

Able to receive s (salt) and B (server public key) correctly from ESP32.

Computing the client proof (M1) on Flutter side and sending it back, but ESP32 rejects it.

Error summary:

ESP32 rejects client proof with Failed to authenticate client proof!

Says Invalid username and/or PoP even though I’m sure the PoP matches.

1.Has anyone successfully implemented ESP32 Security 2 (SRP6) authentication in Flutter?

2.Do I need to hash/encode the PoP in a specific way (e.g., UTF-8 bytes vs. raw string vs. hex) before passing to SRP?

3.How exactly should the username, PoP, and salt be encoded when sending from the Flutter app?

4.Are there any known pitfalls when porting SRP6 client-side calculations (BigInt handling, leading zeros, byte order) to Dart?

Environment:

Flutter 3.19.5

ESP-IDF v5.x

BLE communication using flutter_blue_plus

Any guidance, examples, or working Dart implementations for SRP6 with ESP32 Security2 would be greatly appreciated.

query: How to make Flutter form with type safe and validation that is not messy code?
chunk_content:
Handling complex forms in Flutter can be a major headache. Manual validation, repetitive code for every field, and a lack of "Type-Safety" often make our code messy and full of problems.

That's why I'm very excited to share that I've created a new package called typed_form_fields—a professional and comprehensive package designed to solve these problems once and for all.

Its foundation is the FieldWrapper<T> widget, which lets any Flutter widget transform into a reactive and type-safe form field with minimal effort.

Key Features:
1- Universal & Type-Safe: It transforms any widget into a form field that understands data types like int, bool, and DateTime, eliminating manual parsing.

2- Advanced Validation System: It's not just basic checks; it has built-in support for cross-field validation (like password confirmation) and conditional validation.

3- Fully Dynamic Forms: Need to add a field based on a user's selection or update validation rules from an API? The entire form structure is mutable in real-time.

4- High & Optimized Performance: With debouncing and precise state updates via BLoC, your forms will remain fast and immediately responsive.

5- Production-Ready: It includes more than 7 ready-made widgets, localization for 11 languages, and a robust API for any use case.

I'd be grateful if you try it out, give the repo a star on GitHub, and share your feedback with me. Contributions are open—feel free to fork the package, make your changes, and create a pull request.


<https://pub.dev/packages/typed_form_fields>

query: Hey folks, what was that Flutter todo app demo someone posted recently? Think it had the database persistence stuff - trying to remember which storage solution they used for the project
chunk_content:
​Hello Flutter Community! :wave:
​I'm excited to share my first post here. I've been working on a project to practice my skills and wanted to share the result with you all.
​Flutter To-Do List App with Persistent Local Storage
​I recently integrated my previously built To-Do App with Sqflite :package:, enabling persistent local storage so that tasks are saved even after closing the app. Users can add, edit, and delete tasks, select dates :date: using a calendar picker, and view tasks in colorful :art:, dynamically generated cards for a clean and interactive experience.
​Widgets/Concepts Used
​StatefulWidget & setState :arrows_counterclockwise: for dynamic UI updates
​ListView.builder :clipboard: to render a scrollable list of tasks
​TextField :writing_hand: with TextEditingController for input
​showModalBottomSheet :bellhop_bell: for creating and editing tasks
​showDatePicker :calendar: for selecting dates
​GestureDetector :point_up_2: to handle edit and delete actions
​Container, Row, Column, Expanded, Padding :jigsaw: for structured and responsive layouts
​Sqflite (SQLite) :floppy_disk: for local database storage to persist tasks
​:clapper: Video Demo:
​App in action: adding :pencil2:, editing :memo:, and deleting :x: tasks
​Date picker :date: and colorful dynamic cards :art:
​Database integration :computer: and bottom sheet UI :bellhop_bell:
​:pushpin: Tasks remain saved after restarting the app :arrows_counterclockwise::floppy_disk:
​I'm eager to learn from this amazing community and would greatly appreciate any feedback, suggestions, or advice you might have on my implementation. Thank you for taking the time to check it out!

- the backend sends that email address a link with a unique code in a link
- the user clicks that link that opens the app that processes the deep link by verifying the code and finishing to add the verified email address to the user profile

So in the end, my mechanism works on Android and iOS, but fails miserably on the web. How should I do this?

query: hey so like my flutter app won't connect to this esp32 thing and it keeps saying something about invalid username?? i'm trying to use this security thing but the esp32 just rejects it every time. does the password need to be in a special format or something? i'm not sure what i'm doing wrong with the PoP thing
chunk_content:
Secure connection over ESP32 with Flutter using Security 2 (SRP6) fails – “Failed to authenticate client proof! Invalid username/PoP

I’m working on connecting a Flutter app to an ESP32 device over BLE using the ESP-IDF provisioning/security scheme 2 (SRP6).

I’m trying to establish a secure session with Security 2 using a PoP (Proof of Possession) and salt for SRP verification.

However, the connection fails with the following error messages from the ESP32 logs:

E (xxxxx) security2: Failed to authenticate client proof! E (xxxxx) security2: Received incorrect username and/or PoP for establishing secure session! E (xxxxx) protocomm: Invalid content received, killing connection

What I’ve done:

Using Flutter with flutter_blue_plus to handle BLE communication.

Converted the SRP6 client implementation from Java to Dart to generate A, M, and proof values.

I am passing the correct PoP (same as configured in ESP32) and the salt provided by the device.

Able to receive s (salt) and B (server public key) correctly from ESP32.

Computing the client proof (M1) on Flutter side and sending it back, but ESP32 rejects it.

Error summary:

ESP32 rejects client proof with Failed to authenticate client proof!

Says Invalid username and/or PoP even though I’m sure the PoP matches.

1.Has anyone successfully implemented ESP32 Security 2 (SRP6) authentication in Flutter?

2.Do I need to hash/encode the PoP in a specific way (e.g., UTF-8 bytes vs. raw string vs. hex) before passing to SRP?

3.How exactly should the username, PoP, and salt be encoded when sending from the Flutter app?

4.Are there any known pitfalls when porting SRP6 client-side calculations (BigInt handling, leading zeros, byte order) to Dart?

Environment:

Flutter 3.19.5

ESP-IDF v5.x

BLE communication using flutter_blue_plus

Any guidance, examples, or working Dart implementations for SRP6 with ESP32 Security2 would be greatly appreciated.

query: how do i make forms in flutter that check if the data is right without writing a ton of code for each field
chunk_content:
Handling complex forms in Flutter can be a major headache. Manual validation, repetitive code for every field, and a lack of "Type-Safety" often make our code messy and full of problems.

That's why I'm very excited to share that I've created a new package called typed_form_fields—a professional and comprehensive package designed to solve these problems once and for all.

Its foundation is the FieldWrapper<T> widget, which lets any Flutter widget transform into a reactive and type-safe form field with minimal effort.

Key Features:
1- Universal & Type-Safe: It transforms any widget into a form field that understands data types like int, bool, and DateTime, eliminating manual parsing.

2- Advanced Validation System: It's not just basic checks; it has built-in support for cross-field validation (like password confirmation) and conditional validation.

3- Fully Dynamic Forms: Need to add a field based on a user's selection or update validation rules from an API? The entire form structure is mutable in real-time.

4- High & Optimized Performance: With debouncing and precise state updates via BLoC, your forms will remain fast and immediately responsive.

5- Production-Ready: It includes more than 7 ready-made widgets, localization for 11 languages, and a robust API for any use case.

I'd be grateful if you try it out, give the repo a star on GitHub, and share your feedback with me. Contributions are open—feel free to fork the package, make your changes, and create a pull request.


<https://pub.dev/packages/typed_form_fields>

Today is a special day for me — I’m super excited to share the launch of my first ever web app: SmartDecide :tada:

:point_right: Which laptop should I buy?

:point_right: Should I take this job offer or the other one?

:sparkles: And that’s how SmartDecide was born.

SmartDecide is a free, web-based decision-making platform where you can compare multiple options side by side, set your own priorities (like budget, features, growth potential, or risk level), and instantly get structured recommendations.

It doesn’t replace your intuition — it supports your thinking with clarity and structure.

Handling complex forms in Flutter can be a major headache. Manual validation, repetitive code for every field, and a lack of "Type-Safety" often make our code messy and full of problems.

That's why I'm very excited to share that I've created a new package called typed_form_fields—a professional and comprehensive package designed to solve these problems once and for all.

Its foundation is the FieldWrapper<T> widget, which lets any Flutter widget transform into a reactive and type-safe form field with minimal effort.

Key Features:
1- Universal & Type-Safe: It transforms any widget into a form field that understands data types like int, bool, and DateTime, eliminating manual parsing.

2- Advanced Validation System: It's not just basic checks; it has built-in support for cross-field validation (like password confirmation) and conditional validation.

3- Fully Dynamic Forms: Need to add a field based on a user's selection or update validation rules from an API? The entire form structure is mutable in real-time.

4- High & Optimized Performance: With debouncing and precise state updates via BLoC, your forms will remain fast and immediately responsive.

5- Production-Ready: It includes more than 7 ready-made widgets, localization for 11 languages, and a robust API for any use case.

I'd be grateful if you try it out, give the repo a star on GitHub, and share your feedback with me. Contributions are open—feel free to fork the package, make your changes, and create a pull request.


<https://pub.dev/packages/typed_form_fields>

Handling complex forms in Flutter can be a major headache. Manual validation, repetitive code for every field, and a lack of "Type-Safety" often make our code messy and full of problems.

That's why I'm very excited to share that I've created a new package called typed_form_fields—a professional and comprehensive package designed to solve these problems once and for all.

Its foundation is the FieldWrapper<T> widget, which lets any Flutter widget transform into a reactive and type-safe form field with minimal effort.

Key Features:
1- Universal & Type-Safe: It transforms any widget into a form field that understands data types like int, bool, and DateTime, eliminating manual parsing.

2- Advanced Validation System: It's not just basic checks; it has built-in support for cross-field validation (like password confirmation) and conditional validation.

3- Fully Dynamic Forms: Need to add a field based on a user's selection or update validation rules from an API? The entire form structure is mutable in real-time.

4- High & Optimized Performance: With debouncing and precise state updates via BLoC, your forms will remain fast and immediately responsive.

5- Production-Ready: It includes more than 7 ready-made widgets, localization for 11 languages, and a robust API for any use case.

I'd be grateful if you try it out, give the repo a star on GitHub, and share your feedback with me. Contributions are open—feel free to fork the package, make your changes, and create a pull request.


<https://pub.dev/packages/typed_form_fields>

--------------------------
Project Description: Mobile App Development for Real-Time Dashboard Platform
Overview
We are embarking on a mobile app development project to rebuild and modernize the front end of our real-time dashboard and management platform. The goal is to deliver a highly usable, lightning-fast, and visually consistent mobile application that enables our customers to manage workflows, data tables, and business operations seamlessly on-the-go.

Objectives
• Mobile-First Experience: Redesign the dashboard as a native or cross-platform mobile application, ensuring optimal performance, responsiveness, and accessibility across all iOS and Android devices.
• Modern UI Consistency: Shift from custom, ad-hoc designs to a component-driven approach using established libraries (such as ShadCN, Tailwind UI, etc.), providing a clean, intuitive interface.
• Real-Time Operations: Maintain live updates for tables, lists, modals, and dynamic workflows, allowing instant data visibility and interaction.
• Maintainability & Speed: Build with scalable, maintainable code, ensuring the app can evolve rapidly alongside business needs.
Key Features
• Secure User Authentication: Simple, secure sign-in flows compatible with mobile best practices.
• Dashboard Overview: Real-time visual summaries and notifications of system status.
• Dynamic Data Tables & Lists: Mobile-optimized tables and lists with sorting, filtering, and infinite scrolling.
• Modals & Workflows: Intuitive modal dialogs and step-by-step workflows for critical user actions.
• Push Notifications: Timely alerts for system events, updates, and actionable items.
• Offline Support: Access recent data and continue workflows even with unreliable connectivity.
• Settings & User Profile: Personalizable preferences and user management capabilities.
Technology Stack
• Framework: React Native or Flutter (for cross-platform development), leveraging modern component libraries for consistency and speed.
• Design System: Tailwind UI, ShadCN, or similar, providing a scalable foundation for UI/UX across screens.
• TypeScript: Ensures robust, maintainable code supporting rapid iteration and collaboration.
• State Management: Context API, Redux, or MobX for dependable and scalable state handling.
Collaboration & Workflow
• Agile Iterations: Ship daily improvements—functionality and polish will be incrementally rolled out based on real user feedback.
• Transparent Communication: Frequent updates, collaborative backlog grooming, and accessible progress tracking.
• Rapid Prototyping: Use of AI tools and low-code solutions (e.g., <http://V0.dev|V0.dev>) to accelerate component delivery and experimentation.
• Focus on Usability: Prioritize intuitive interactions, mobile-first layouts, and accessible design throughout the app.
Target Users
• Business customers who rely on their mobile devices to manage, monitor, and interact with dashboards and operational interfaces in real time.
• Users who value speed, reliability, and a polished, professional app experience.
Success Metrics
• Improved user engagement and satisfaction on mobile platforms.
• Reduction in support queries related to usability or mobile access issues.
• Faster mobile development cycles, enabling quick adaptation to changing business requirements.
---------------------

Project Description: Mobile App Development for Real-Time Dashboard Platform
Overview
We are embarking on a mobile app development project to rebuild and modernize the front end of our real-time dashboard and management platform. The goal is to deliver a highly usable, lightning-fast, and visually consistent mobile application that enables our customers to manage workflows, data tables, and business operations seamlessly on-the-go.

Objectives
• Mobile-First Experience: Redesign the dashboard as a native or cross-platform mobile application, ensuring optimal performance, responsiveness, and accessibility across all iOS and Android devices.
• Modern UI Consistency: Shift from custom, ad-hoc designs to a component-driven approach using established libraries (such as ShadCN, Tailwind UI, etc.), providing a clean, intuitive interface.
• Real-Time Operations: Maintain live updates for tables, lists, modals, and dynamic workflows, allowing instant data visibility and interaction.
• Maintainability & Speed: Build with scalable, maintainable code, ensuring the app can evolve rapidly alongside business needs.
Key Features
• Secure User Authentication: Simple, secure sign-in flows compatible with mobile best practices.
• Dashboard Overview: Real-time visual summaries and notifications of system status.
• Dynamic Data Tables & Lists: Mobile-optimized tables and lists with sorting, filtering, and infinite scrolling.
• Modals & Workflows: Intuitive modal dialogs and step-by-step workflows for critical user actions.
• Push Notifications: Timely alerts for system events, updates, and actionable items.
• Offline Support: Access recent data and continue workflows even with unreliable connectivity.
• Settings & User Profile: Personalizable preferences and user management capabilities.
Technology Stack
• Framework: React Native or Flutter (for cross-platform development), leveraging modern component libraries for consistency and speed.
• Design System: Tailwind UI, ShadCN, or similar, providing a scalable foundation for UI/UX across screens.
• TypeScript: Ensures robust, maintainable code supporting rapid iteration and collaboration.
• State Management: Context API, Redux, or MobX for dependable and scalable state handling.
Collaboration & Workflow
• Agile Iterations: Ship daily improvements—functionality and polish will be incrementally rolled out based on real user feedback.
• Transparent Communication: Frequent updates, collaborative backlog grooming, and accessible progress tracking.
• Rapid Prototyping: Use of AI tools and low-code solutions (e.g., <http://V0.dev|V0.dev>) to accelerate component delivery and experimentation.
• Focus on Usability: Prioritize intuitive interactions, mobile-first layouts, and accessible design throughout the app.
Target Users
• Business customers who rely on their mobile devices to manage, monitor, and interact with dashboards and operational interfaces in real time.
• Users who value speed, reliability, and a polished, professional app experience.
Success Metrics
• Improved user engagement and satisfaction on mobile platforms.
• Reduction in support queries related to usability or mobile access issues.
• Faster mobile development cycles, enabling quick adaptation to changing business requirements.
